title: Time Limits on Using Education Benefits
content:
**Regulatory digest — delimiting dates under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education).**

The delimiting date is the last date on which a benefit can be used; a benefit with no time limit carries no delimiting date, and a benefit whose delimiting date has passed is delimited.

**Clause 1 — retired.** "A benefit with a delimiting date pays nothing for training after that date" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the delimiting cut-off of a month's payment.

**Clause 2 — in force.** A tier whose delimiting period is 0 years has no time limit. This covers the Forever GI Bill for veterans separated on or after January 1, 2013, and Chapter 35 for children who turned 18 on or after August 1, 2023.

**Clause 3 — retired.** "The delimiting date of Chapter 30 runs 10 years (the tier's delimiting period) from the last release from active duty" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for working out a delimiting extension. The tier figures themselves are unchanged.

**Clause 4 — retired.** "A term that straddles the delimiting date is paid only through that date" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the delimiting cut-off.

**Clause 2 illustrated (hypothetical).**

| Beneficiary | Time limit under Clause 2 |
|---|---|
| Veteran separated on January 1, 2013, holding the Post-9/11 GI Bill | None |
| Child who turned 18 on August 1, 2023, holding Chapter 35 | None |

superseded_clauses: A benefit with a delimiting date pays nothing for training after that date
The delimiting date of Chapter 30 runs delimiting_years years from the last release from active duty.
A term that straddles the delimiting date is paid only through that date.
